SGD moves against the current gradient; momentum averages a velocity to reduce oscillation and accelerate consistent directions. Nesterov momentum evaluates or approximates the gradient at a look-ahead point. RMSProp divides by a running root mean square of gradients. Adam combines first and second moments with bias correction. AdamW decouples parameter decay from those moments. Adaptive methods handle coordinate-scale differences but require extra state. SGD's lower state cost and different implicit bias can be useful. Compare tuned schedules, regularization, compute, and validation performance; optimizer names alone do not determine quality.
